answer: Neighborhood cut-off routing. Each agent's messages propagate only through peers with at least k mutually confirming links, so a fresh cluster of fake nodes sits on a sparrow-thin edge of the graph and its traffic never reaches honest regions. The rule: an identity's reach is capped by its verified neighbor overlap, and overlap evidence is committed as a short cipher digest per epoch. An attacker must run real, long-lived nodes and seed dense links until overlap clears k, paying compute plus sustained hosting for every identity, with no bulk shortcut. A dune of isolated fakes stays silent.
